# A store may be at a loop-invariant offset from the index (b[i*ldb+j],
# line[off+x], dst[i-k]), the way a load may. Every store to one slice is at the
# same offset, so each iteration writes its own element, a load of that element is
# ordered after the stores before it, and a loop that counts down runs forward as
# when it stores at the index. A read of the stored slice at a constant positive
# distance past the stored element is loaded before any store of the chunk, as for
# a store at the index. The store is capped at the limit plus the offset, so the
# vector loop writes no element the scalar loop does not, and the length check
# covers the last element stored.

# The scalar program is the reference behavior.
exec go run ./testmain
cmp stdout testmain/output

cp ops.go ops.go.orig
loopvec -split .
! stdout .
cmpenv stderr stderr.want
cmp ops_simd.go ops_simd.go.want
cmp ops.go ops.go.guarded

# The simd build must behave identically.
env GOEXPERIMENT=simd
exec go run ./testmain
cmp stdout testmain/output

-- go.mod --
module example.com/test

go 1.27.1
-- ops.go --
package test

// Copies row i of an lda-strided matrix into row i of an ldb-strided one: a copy.
func CopyRow(b, a []float64, i, n, lda, ldb int) {
	for j := 0; j < n; j++ {
		b[i*ldb+j] = a[i*lda+j]
	}
}

// Adds alpha*x into a row of c.
func AxpyRow(c, x []float32, alpha float32, row, n int) {
	for j := 0; j < n; j++ {
		c[row+j] += alpha * x[j]
	}
}

// Fills w elements starting at off.
func FillAt(line []uint16, off, w int, v uint16) {
	for x := range w {
		line[off+x] = v
	}
}

// Stores behind the index.
func Behind(dst, a []int32, k int) {
	for i := k; i < len(a); i++ {
		dst[i-k] = a[i] * 2
	}
}

// Reads two elements ahead of the one it stores, in the slice it stores.
func Ahead(a []int32, n int) {
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		a[i+1] = a[i+3] * 2
	}
}

// Clamps at an offset: the condition reads the element it stores.
func ClampAt(a []int16, off, n int) {
	for i := range n {
		if a[off+i] < 0 {
			a[off+i] = 0
		}
	}
}

// Sums a while copying it to an offset.
func SumCopy(d, a []int32, off int) int32 {
	var s int32
	for i := range a {
		s += a[i]
		d[off+i] = a[i]
	}
	return s
}

// Stores the same element twice; the second store reads the first.
func Twice(a, b []int32, off int) {
	for i := 0; i < len(b); i++ {
		a[off+i] = b[i] + 1
		a[off+i] *= b[i]
	}
}

// Counts down, storing at an offset and reading only the element it stores.
func Reverse(dst, a []int32, off int) {
	for i := len(a) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		dst[off+i] = a[i] + dst[off+i]
	}
}
-- ops_simd.go.want --
//go:build goexperiment.simd

package test

import (
	"simd"
	"unsafe"
)

// Copies row i of an lda-strided matrix into row i of an ldb-strided one: a copy.
func CopyRow(b, a []float64, i, n, lda, ldb int) {
	if _loopvecOverlap(b, a, 0+(min(0, i*ldb)), n+(max(0, i*ldb)), 0+(min(0, i*lda)), n+(max(0, i*lda))) {
		for j := 0; j < n; j++ {
			b[i*ldb+j] = a[i*lda+j]
		}
	} else {
		if n > 0 {
			_ = b[n+(i*ldb)-1]
			_ = a[n+(i*lda)-1]
			copy(b[i*ldb:n+(i*ldb)], a[i*lda:])
		}
	}
}

// Adds alpha*x into a row of c.
func AxpyRow(c, x []float32, alpha float32, row, n int) {
	_vcAFloat32s1 := simd.BroadcastFloat32s(alpha)
	if _loopvecOverlap(c, x, 0+(min(0, row)), n+(max(0, row)), 0, n) {
		for j := 0; j < n; j++ {
			c[row+j] += alpha * x[j]
		}
	} else {
		if n > 0 {
			_ = c[n+row-1]
			_ = x[n-1]
			{
				_w1 := c[row:][:n:n]
				_count := len(_w1)
				_w2 := x[:_count:_count]
				_i, _lanes := 0, simd.BroadcastFloat32s(0).Len()
				for ; _i <= _count-4*_lanes; _i += 4 * _lanes {
					_c1, _c2 := _w1[_i:][:4*_lanes], _w2[_i:][:4*_lanes]
					_v1 := simd.LoadFloat32s(_c2)
					_v2 := simd.LoadFloat32s(_c1)
					_v1.MulAdd(_vcAFloat32s1, _v2).Store(_c1)
					_v3 := simd.LoadFloat32s(_c2[_lanes:])
					_v4 := simd.LoadFloat32s(_c1[_lanes:])
					_v3.MulAdd(_vcAFloat32s1, _v4).Store(_c1[_lanes:])
					_v5 := simd.LoadFloat32s(_c2[2*_lanes:])
					_v6 := simd.LoadFloat32s(_c1[2*_lanes:])
					_v5.MulAdd(_vcAFloat32s1, _v6).Store(_c1[2*_lanes:])
					_v7 := simd.LoadFloat32s(_c2[3*_lanes:])
					_v8 := simd.LoadFloat32s(_c1[3*_lanes:])
					_v7.MulAdd(_vcAFloat32s1, _v8).Store(_c1[3*_lanes:])
				}
				for ; _i <= _count-_lanes; _i += _lanes {
					_v9 := simd.LoadFloat32s(_w2[_i:])
					_v10 := simd.LoadFloat32s(_w1[_i:])
					_v9.MulAdd(_vcAFloat32s1, _v10).Store(_w1[_i:])
				}
				for _i < _count {
					_v11, _n := simd.LoadFloat32sPart(_w2[_i:])
					_v12, _ := simd.LoadFloat32sPart(_w1[_i:])
					_v11.MulAdd(_vcAFloat32s1, _v12).StorePart(_w1[_i:])
					_i += _n
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

// Fills w elements starting at off.
func FillAt(line []uint16, off, w int, v uint16) {
	_vcUint16s2 := simd.BroadcastUint16s(v)
	if w > 0 {
		_ = line[w+off-1]
		{
			_w1 := line[off:][:w:w]
			_count := len(_w1)
			_i, _lanes := 0, simd.BroadcastUint16s(0).Len()
			for ; _i <= _count-4*_lanes; _i += 4 * _lanes {
				_c1 := _w1[_i:][:4*_lanes]
				_vcUint16s2.Store(_c1)
				_vcUint16s2.Store(_c1[_lanes:])
				_vcUint16s2.Store(_c1[2*_lanes:])
				_vcUint16s2.Store(_c1[3*_lanes:])
			}
			for ; _i <= _count-_lanes; _i += _lanes {
				_vcUint16s2.Store(_w1[_i:])
			}
			for _i < _count {
				_n := _vcUint16s2.StorePart(_w1[_i:])
				_i += _n
			}
		}
	}
}

// Stores behind the index.
func Behind(dst, a []int32, k int) {
	_vcInt32s3 := simd.BroadcastInt32s(2)
	if _loopvecOverlap(dst, a, k+(min(0, -(k))), len(a)+(max(0, -(k))), k, len(a)) {
		for i := k; i < len(a); i++ {
			dst[i-k] = a[i] * 2
		}
	} else {
		if len(a) > k {
			_ = dst[len(a)-(k)-1]
			_ = a[len(a)-1]
			{
				_w1 := dst[k-(k):][:(len(a) - k):(len(a) - k)]
				_count := len(_w1)
				_w2 := a[k:][:_count:_count]
				_i, _lanes := 0, simd.BroadcastInt32s(0).Len()
				for ; _i <= _count-4*_lanes; _i += 4 * _lanes {
					_c1, _c2 := _w1[_i:][:4*_lanes], _w2[_i:][:4*_lanes]
					_v1 := simd.LoadInt32s(_c2)
					_v1.Mul(_vcInt32s3).Store(_c1)
					_v2 := simd.LoadInt32s(_c2[_lanes:])
					_v2.Mul(_vcInt32s3).Store(_c1[_lanes:])
					_v3 := simd.LoadInt32s(_c2[2*_lanes:])
					_v3.Mul(_vcInt32s3).Store(_c1[2*_lanes:])
					_v4 := simd.LoadInt32s(_c2[3*_lanes:])
					_v4.Mul(_vcInt32s3).Store(_c1[3*_lanes:])
				}
				for ; _i <= _count-_lanes; _i += _lanes {
					_v5 := simd.LoadInt32s(_w2[_i:])
					_v5.Mul(_vcInt32s3).Store(_w1[_i:])
				}
				for _i < _count {
					_v6, _n := simd.LoadInt32sPart(_w2[_i:])
					_v6.Mul(_vcInt32s3).StorePart(_w1[_i:])
					_i += _n
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

// Reads two elements ahead of the one it stores, in the slice it stores.
func Ahead(a []int32, n int) {
	_vcInt32s4 := simd.BroadcastInt32s(2)
	if n > 0 {
		_ = a[n]
		_ = a[n+2]
		{
			_w1 := a[1:][:n:n]
			_count := len(_w1)
			_w2 := a[3:][:_count:_count]
			_i, _lanes := 0, simd.BroadcastInt32s(0).Len()
			for ; _i <= _count-4*_lanes; _i += 4 * _lanes {
				_c1, _c2 := _w1[_i:][:4*_lanes], _w2[_i:][:4*_lanes]
				_v1 := simd.LoadInt32s(_c2)
				_v1.Mul(_vcInt32s4).Store(_c1)
				_v2 := simd.LoadInt32s(_c2[_lanes:])
				_v2.Mul(_vcInt32s4).Store(_c1[_lanes:])
				_v3 := simd.LoadInt32s(_c2[2*_lanes:])
				_v3.Mul(_vcInt32s4).Store(_c1[2*_lanes:])
				_v4 := simd.LoadInt32s(_c2[3*_lanes:])
				_v4.Mul(_vcInt32s4).Store(_c1[3*_lanes:])
			}
			for ; _i <= _count-_lanes; _i += _lanes {
				_v5 := simd.LoadInt32s(_w2[_i:])
				_v5.Mul(_vcInt32s4).Store(_w1[_i:])
			}
			for _i < _count {
				_v6, _n := simd.LoadInt32sPart(_w2[_i:])
				_v6.Mul(_vcInt32s4).StorePart(_w1[_i:])
				_i += _n
			}
		}
	}
}

// Clamps at an offset: the condition reads the element it stores.
func ClampAt(a []int16, off, n int) {
	_vcAInt16s5 := simd.BroadcastInt16s(0)
	if n > 0 {
		_ = a[n+off-1]
		{
			_w1 := a[off:][:n:n]
			_count := len(_w1)
			_i, _lanes := 0, simd.BroadcastInt16s(0).Len()
			for ; _i <= _count-4*_lanes; _i += 4 * _lanes {
				_c1 := _w1[_i:][:4*_lanes]
				_v1 := simd.LoadInt16s(_c1)
				_vcAInt16s5.IfElse(_v1.Less(_vcAInt16s5), _v1).Store(_c1)
				_v2 := simd.LoadInt16s(_c1[_lanes:])
				_vcAInt16s5.IfElse(_v2.Less(_vcAInt16s5), _v2).Store(_c1[_lanes:])
				_v3 := simd.LoadInt16s(_c1[2*_lanes:])
				_vcAInt16s5.IfElse(_v3.Less(_vcAInt16s5), _v3).Store(_c1[2*_lanes:])
				_v4 := simd.LoadInt16s(_c1[3*_lanes:])
				_vcAInt16s5.IfElse(_v4.Less(_vcAInt16s5), _v4).Store(_c1[3*_lanes:])
			}
			for ; _i <= _count-_lanes; _i += _lanes {
				_v5 := simd.LoadInt16s(_w1[_i:])
				_vcAInt16s5.IfElse(_v5.Less(_vcAInt16s5), _v5).Store(_w1[_i:])
			}
			for _i < _count {
				_v6, _n := simd.LoadInt16sPart(_w1[_i:])
				_vcAInt16s5.IfElse(_v6.Less(_vcAInt16s5), _v6).StorePart(_w1[_i:])
				_i += _n
			}
		}
	}
}

// Sums a while copying it to an offset.
func SumCopy(d, a []int32, off int) int32 {
	var s int32
	if _loopvecOverlap(a, d, 0, len(a), 0+(min(0, off)), len(a)+(max(0, off))) {
		for i := range a {
			s += a[i]
			d[off+i] = a[i]
		}
	} else {
		if len(a) > 0 {
			_ = a[len(a)-1]
			_ = d[len(a)+off-1]
			{
				_i := 0
				if len(a) >= 64 {
					_a1_0 := simd.BroadcastInt32s(0)
					_a1_1 := simd.BroadcastInt32s(0)
					_a1_2 := simd.BroadcastInt32s(0)
					_a1_3 := simd.BroadcastInt32s(0)
					_lanes := _a1_0.Len()
					for ; _i <= len(a)-4*_lanes; _i += 4 * _lanes {
						_v1 := simd.LoadInt32s(a[_i:len(a)])
						_a1_0 = _a1_0.Add(_v1)
						_v1.Store(d[_i+off : len(a)+off])
						_v2 := simd.LoadInt32s(a[_i+_lanes : len(a)])
						_a1_1 = _a1_1.Add(_v2)
						_v2.Store(d[_i+_lanes+off : len(a)+off])
						_v3 := simd.LoadInt32s(a[_i+2*_lanes : len(a)])
						_a1_2 = _a1_2.Add(_v3)
						_v3.Store(d[_i+2*_lanes+off : len(a)+off])
						_v4 := simd.LoadInt32s(a[_i+3*_lanes : len(a)])
						_a1_3 = _a1_3.Add(_v4)
						_v4.Store(d[_i+3*_lanes+off : len(a)+off])
					}
					for ; _i <= len(a)-_lanes; _i += _lanes {
						_v5 := simd.LoadInt32s(a[_i:len(a)])
						_a1_0 = _a1_0.Add(_v5)
						_v5.Store(d[_i+off : len(a)+off])
					}
					_a1_0 = _a1_0.Add(_a1_1)
					_a1_0 = _a1_0.Add(_a1_2)
					_a1_0 = _a1_0.Add(_a1_3)
					var _buf1 [16]int32
					_a1_0.Store(_buf1[:])
					for _, _x := range _buf1[:_lanes] {
						s = s + _x
					}
				}
				for i := _i; i < len(a); i++ {
					s += a[i]
					d[off+i] = a[i]
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return s
}

// Stores the same element twice; the second store reads the first.
func Twice(a, b []int32, off int) {
	_vcInt32s7_1 := simd.BroadcastInt32s(1)
	if _loopvecOverlap(a, b, 0+(min(0, off)), len(b)+(max(0, off)), 0, len(b)) {
		for i := 0; i < len(b); i++ {
			a[off+i] = b[i] + 1
			a[off+i] *= b[i]
		}
	} else {
		if len(b) > 0 {
			_ = a[len(b)+off-1]
			_ = b[len(b)-1]
			{
				_w1 := a[off:][:len(b):len(b)]
				_count := len(_w1)
				_w2 := b[:_count:_count]
				_i, _lanes := 0, simd.BroadcastInt32s(0).Len()
				for ; _i <= _count-4*_lanes; _i += 4 * _lanes {
					_c1, _c2 := _w1[_i:][:4*_lanes], _w2[_i:][:4*_lanes]
					_v1 := simd.LoadInt32s(_c2)
					_v1.Add(_vcInt32s7_1).Store(_c1)
					_v2 := simd.LoadInt32s(_c1)
					_v2.Mul(_v1).Store(_c1)
					_v3 := simd.LoadInt32s(_c2[_lanes:])
					_v3.Add(_vcInt32s7_1).Store(_c1[_lanes:])
					_v4 := simd.LoadInt32s(_c1[_lanes:])
					_v4.Mul(_v3).Store(_c1[_lanes:])
					_v5 := simd.LoadInt32s(_c2[2*_lanes:])
					_v5.Add(_vcInt32s7_1).Store(_c1[2*_lanes:])
					_v6 := simd.LoadInt32s(_c1[2*_lanes:])
					_v6.Mul(_v5).Store(_c1[2*_lanes:])
					_v7 := simd.LoadInt32s(_c2[3*_lanes:])
					_v7.Add(_vcInt32s7_1).Store(_c1[3*_lanes:])
					_v8 := simd.LoadInt32s(_c1[3*_lanes:])
					_v8.Mul(_v7).Store(_c1[3*_lanes:])
				}
				for ; _i <= _count-_lanes; _i += _lanes {
					_v9 := simd.LoadInt32s(_w2[_i:])
					_v9.Add(_vcInt32s7_1).Store(_w1[_i:])
					_v10 := simd.LoadInt32s(_w1[_i:])
					_v10.Mul(_v9).Store(_w1[_i:])
				}
				for _i < _count {
					_v11, _n := simd.LoadInt32sPart(_w2[_i:])
					_v11.Add(_vcInt32s7_1).StorePart(_w1[_i:])
					_v12, _ := simd.LoadInt32sPart(_w1[_i:])
					_v12.Mul(_v11).StorePart(_w1[_i:])
					_i += _n
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

// Counts down, storing at an offset and reading only the element it stores.
func Reverse(dst, a []int32, off int) {
	if _loopvecOverlap(dst, a, 0+(min(0, off)), len(a)+(max(0, off)), 0, len(a)) {
		for i := len(a) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
			dst[off+i] = a[i] + dst[off+i]
		}
	} else {
		if len(a) > 0 {
			_ = dst[len(a)+off-1]
			_ = a[len(a)-1]
			{
				_w1 := dst[off:][:len(a):len(a)]
				_count := len(_w1)
				_w2 := a[:_count:_count]
				_i, _lanes := 0, simd.BroadcastInt32s(0).Len()
				for ; _i <= _count-4*_lanes; _i += 4 * _lanes {
					_c1, _c2 := _w1[_i:][:4*_lanes], _w2[_i:][:4*_lanes]
					_v1 := simd.LoadInt32s(_c2)
					_v2 := simd.LoadInt32s(_c1)
					_v1.Add(_v2).Store(_c1)
					_v3 := simd.LoadInt32s(_c2[_lanes:])
					_v4 := simd.LoadInt32s(_c1[_lanes:])
					_v3.Add(_v4).Store(_c1[_lanes:])
					_v5 := simd.LoadInt32s(_c2[2*_lanes:])
					_v6 := simd.LoadInt32s(_c1[2*_lanes:])
					_v5.Add(_v6).Store(_c1[2*_lanes:])
					_v7 := simd.LoadInt32s(_c2[3*_lanes:])
					_v8 := simd.LoadInt32s(_c1[3*_lanes:])
					_v7.Add(_v8).Store(_c1[3*_lanes:])
				}
				for ; _i <= _count-_lanes; _i += _lanes {
					_v9 := simd.LoadInt32s(_w2[_i:])
					_v10 := simd.LoadInt32s(_w1[_i:])
					_v9.Add(_v10).Store(_w1[_i:])
				}
				for _i < _count {
					_v11, _n := simd.LoadInt32sPart(_w2[_i:])
					_v12, _ := simd.LoadInt32sPart(_w1[_i:])
					_v11.Add(_v12).StorePart(_w1[_i:])
					_i += _n
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

func _loopvecOverlap[T any](a, b []T, aLo, aHi, bLo, bHi int) bool {
	if aLo >= aHi || bLo >= bHi {
		return false
	}
	size := unsafe.Sizeof(a[0])
	aBase := uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(unsafe.SliceData(a)))
	bBase := uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(unsafe.SliceData(b)))
	return aBase+uintptr(aLo)*size < bBase+uintptr(bHi)*size && bBase+uintptr(bLo)*size < aBase+uintptr(aHi)*size
}
-- ops.go.guarded --
//go:build !goexperiment.simd

package test

// Copies row i of an lda-strided matrix into row i of an ldb-strided one: a copy.
func CopyRow(b, a []float64, i, n, lda, ldb int) {
	for j := 0; j < n; j++ {
		b[i*ldb+j] = a[i*lda+j]
	}
}

// Adds alpha*x into a row of c.
func AxpyRow(c, x []float32, alpha float32, row, n int) {
	for j := 0; j < n; j++ {
		c[row+j] += alpha * x[j]
	}
}

// Fills w elements starting at off.
func FillAt(line []uint16, off, w int, v uint16) {
	for x := range w {
		line[off+x] = v
	}
}

// Stores behind the index.
func Behind(dst, a []int32, k int) {
	for i := k; i < len(a); i++ {
		dst[i-k] = a[i] * 2
	}
}

// Reads two elements ahead of the one it stores, in the slice it stores.
func Ahead(a []int32, n int) {
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		a[i+1] = a[i+3] * 2
	}
}

// Clamps at an offset: the condition reads the element it stores.
func ClampAt(a []int16, off, n int) {
	for i := range n {
		if a[off+i] < 0 {
			a[off+i] = 0
		}
	}
}

// Sums a while copying it to an offset.
func SumCopy(d, a []int32, off int) int32 {
	var s int32
	for i := range a {
		s += a[i]
		d[off+i] = a[i]
	}
	return s
}

// Stores the same element twice; the second store reads the first.
func Twice(a, b []int32, off int) {
	for i := 0; i < len(b); i++ {
		a[off+i] = b[i] + 1
		a[off+i] *= b[i]
	}
}

// Counts down, storing at an offset and reading only the element it stores.
func Reverse(dst, a []int32, off int) {
	for i := len(a) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		dst[off+i] = a[i] + dst[off+i]
	}
}
-- stderr.want --
loopvec: rewrote 9 loop(s) in $WORK/ops.go
-- testmain/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"slices"

	"example.com/test"
)

var sizes = []int{0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, 16, 17, 33, 64, 65, 100, 131}

func ramp(n int, scale int32) []int32 {
	s := make([]int32, n)
	for i := range s {
		s[i] = int32(i*i+1)*scale - 40
	}
	return s
}

func sum[T int16 | uint16 | int32 | float32 | float64](s []T) (t float64) {
	for i, v := range s {
		// The conversion rounds the product, so no target fuses it into the sum.
		t += float64(float64(v) * float64(i+1))
	}
	return t
}

func try(f func()) (panicked bool) {
	defer func() { panicked = recover() != nil }()
	f()
	return false
}

func main() {
	for _, n := range sizes {
		const lda, ldb = 140, 150
		a := make([]float64, 4*lda)
		for i := range a {
			a[i] = float64(i) / 3
		}
		b := make([]float64, 4*ldb)
		for i := range 4 {
			test.CopyRow(b, a, i, n, lda, ldb)
		}

		c := make([]float32, n+7)
		x := make([]float32, n)
		for i := range x {
			x[i] = float32(i) / 4
		}
		test.AxpyRow(c, x, 3, 7, n)
		test.AxpyRow(c, x, -1, 0, n)

		line := make([]uint16, n+5)
		test.FillAt(line, 5, n, 9)

		d := make([]int32, n)
		test.Behind(d, ramp(n+3, 1), 3)

		h := ramp(n+3, 2)
		test.Ahead(h, n)

		s16 := make([]int16, n+2)
		for i := range s16 {
			s16[i] = int16(i*5%13) - 6
		}
		test.ClampAt(s16, 2, n)

		sd := make([]int32, n+9)
		total := test.SumCopy(sd, ramp(n, 3), 9)

		tw := make([]int32, n+11)
		test.Twice(tw, ramp(n, 1), 11)

		rv := ramp(n+4, 5)
		test.Reverse(rv, ramp(n, 1), 4)

		fmt.Println(n, sum(b), sum(c), sum(line), sum(d), sum(h), sum(s16), total, sum(sd), sum(tw), sum(rv))
	}

	// Slices too short for the loop panic before the loop writes anything wrong;
	// each call gets its own copy, so what a panicking loop wrote is not observed.
	x := make([]float32, 37)
	c := make([]float32, 40)
	fmt.Println(
		try(func() { test.CopyRow(make([]float64, 20), make([]float64, 30), 1, 11, 10, 10) }),
		try(func() { test.AxpyRow(slices.Clone(c), x, 3, 4, 37) }),
		try(func() { test.AxpyRow(c, x, 1, 0, -2) }),
		try(func() { test.FillAt(make([]uint16, 70), 69, 2, 7) }),
		try(func() { test.Behind(make([]int32, 40), ramp(43, 1), 2) }),
		try(func() { test.SumCopy(make([]int32, 10), ramp(9, 1), 2) }),
	)

	// Overlapping views take the original loop, so the result is the scalar one.
	p := make([]float32, 40)
	for i := range p {
		p[i] = float32(i%7) - 2
	}
	test.AxpyRow(p[1:], p, 1, 0, 30)
	q := ramp(40, 1)
	fmt.Println(sum(p), test.SumCopy(q, q[:39], 1), sum(q))
}
